**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic Number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Isotopic Forms** |
• ¹H (protium) – most abundant (~99.98%)
• ²H (deuterium) – ~0.02% natural abundance
• ³H (tritium) – radioactive, very rare (<10⁻⁹ ppm) | | **Standard Atomic Weight** | 1.00794 u (weighted average including isotopes) | | **Electron Configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **Ionization Energy** | 13.598 eV (first IE) | | **Electron Affinity** | –72 kJ/mol (negative → no stable negative ion under normal conditions) | | **Boiling Point (STP)** | –252.87 °C (121 K) | | **Melting Point (STP)** | –259.16 °C (14 K) | | **Density (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g/L (≈9×10⁻⁵ kg/m³) – lightest element/gas | | **Molar Volume (ideal gas, 273 K, 1 atm)** | ≈22.414 L/mol | | **State at Room Temperature** | Diatomic gaseous molecule (H₂) | | **Bond Dissociation Energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol | | **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a proton donor (acidic); forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution. In organic chemistry, behaves as a weak base when forming alkyl or aryl halides via SN1/SN2 mechanisms. | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive as a reducing agent; burns readily in air producing water vapor: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. Combines explosively with oxygen over a wide range of concentrations (5–75 %). | | **Solubility in Water** | Very low (~8.7 mg per liter at 25 °C) due to non‑polarity. | | **Spectroscopic Features** | Strong absorption in UV-visible region (Lyman series lines around 91 nm). Infrared active vibrational mode near 4400 cm⁻¹ (for H₂). | | **Chemical Behavior** | • Forms covalent bonds with many elements (e.g., C, N, O).
• Participates in metal hydride formation (ex: NaBH₄, LiAlH₄).
• Can act as ligand in organometallic complexes (η²‑H₂ coordination). | | **Physical Uses** | Fuel (rocket propellant, fuel cells), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, methanol production), cryogenic cooling (liquid hydrogen). | | **Biological Role** | Essential component of amino acids, nucleobases, ATP hydrolysis; involved in metabolic pathways like glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. | ### Quick Takeaways * **Lightweight:** At room temperature it’s the least dense substance known—about one‑tenth the density of helium. * **Highly Reactive Gas:** Burns instantly in air; explosive mixtures possible from 5 % to 75 % H₂ in O₂. * **Simple Molecule:** Two protons share two electrons; the H–H bond is strong yet easily broken during combustion or catalytic reactions. * **Versatile Chemistry:** From simple diatomics to complex organometallics, hydrogen participates across all branches of chemistry—from inorganic salts to biochemistry. * **Energy Carrier:** Central to clean-energy technologies such as PEM fuel cells where H₂ reacts electrochemically to generate electricity and only water as waste product. Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What are the different properties of Hydrogen?" They want an answer about hydrogen's properties. We can provide physical and chemical properties: atomic weight, electronegativity, ionization energy, electron affinity, boiling/ melting points, density, etc. Also isotopes H1, D2, T3.

We might also mention its behavior as gas at STP, flammability, uses, bonding characteristics (H-H single bond), ability to form hydrides with metals, acid-base behavior (hydrogen ions). Provide some key data values.
